replies.author: BrianScottGregory
replies.body:
Can't say I agree. Just last week I was working with MCP connections via a local AI to GIMP and Blender, doing 2D and 3D imagery the same exact way a real user would by having the AI use the same tools a user would to draw the image I define. 

Now while the results sucked - for now - the models I can use on an average user's computer like my own can do imagery - but for now - it sucks. Here's an example of a simple flower I had AI paint on my system in GIMP. 

https://preview.redd.it/00jgcf9uzlrh1.png?width=512&format=png&auto=webp&s=c9dcad8b1cb83e497013579e676cca292debac94

Like a child's art, right?

But here's the thing. The imagery you're seeing is one form of AI art using image aggregation, where there's other approaches to AI art like that which I'm researching - literally using the same tools to create the art that an artist would. 

So when you say "AI art is bad". You're only seeing AI producing art and imagery in one specific way. That's a bit like looking at watercolor on canvas and saying "I hate AI art" when what you're really saying is "I don't like this type of (watercolor) art", for no other reason than you're not aware there are other applications to create art using AI that literally mirror human processes like the art that was generated with a tool like the one I'm working on. 

When there reaches a point in the very near future - what I'm working on - where art can be created a completely different way - the same way humans do it... 

Are you still going to be hating it?

Or are you just going to hate on principle because you hate AI?

I think we both know the answer to that question, don't we?

comments.author: Equal-Border-7793
comments.body: However, looking at the video as a whole, the placement of roadside assets feels a bit off; you might need to carefully refine the generation rules. The game content also seems somewhat lacking—you need elements that stir up player emotions, such as adding elderly ladies who dash recklessly across the street (at high speed), or introducing shooting mechanics and hostile creatures to give players something to do. You’ll also want to incorporate some in-game progression systems; planning these out before you start building will yield much better results than simply asking AI to generate everything on the fly. Finally, give the game a simple, clear main storyline and a romance arc (perhaps incorporating your own real-life love story would add a touch of authenticity). P.S. If the demo gets a good reception, I’d suggest hiring someone else to handle the music—the current tracks are honestly terrible.
